summary.text: A 50-year-old never smoker with no significant past medical history and not on any medications presented with jaundice and abdominal distension. CT showed diffuse hepatomegaly and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Serum biochemistry showed elevated hepatobiliary enzymes, T-Bil 4.1 mg/dL and Child-Pugh Grade C, with markedly elevated CEA, NSE and CA19-9.

EBUS-TBNA of the mediastinal lymph nodes showed malignant cells positive for TTF-1 with strong ALK positivity, and the Amoy lung cancer panel detected an ALK fusion, confirming ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma, clinical stage IVB. At initial presentation the performance status was 3 with liver failure due to diffuse liver metastasis.

Alectinib was started at 150 mg and escalated to 300 mg then 600 mg, but abdominal distension did not improve and T-Bil rose to 24.1 mg/dL while worsening anemia required transfusions. Fragmented red cells, reticulocytes 19.1‰, a negative Coombs test, low haptoglobin and ADAMTS13 activity above 10% led to a diagnosis of alectinib-induced hemolytic anemia, and treatment was switched to oral lorlatinib 50 mg.

After the switch, anemia improved and T-Bil decreased. Over approximately 6 months imaging showed reduced hepatomegaly and improved intrahepatic necrosis, Child-Pugh class improved from C to A and PS became 0. A liver biopsy confirmed liver metastasis. Lorlatinib 75 mg caused grade 2 peripheral neuropathy, so 50 mg was maintained, and the patient can currently continue lorlatinib.
